svg.text: Three Functions, Three Abstraction Layers: NUMA Node / Section / Zone
Question: "Which physical memory belongs to which CPU cluster?"
Question: "How to efficiently manage struct page for non-contiguous physical memory?"
Physical address space divided into 128MB sections:
Each section gets a struct page array in VMEMMAP:
Key: Only present sections get struct page arrays allocated. Holes are skipped = no memory wasted.
Question: "How to satisfy different DMA address constraints for different devices?"
Node 0 physical address range divided into zones:
Layer 4: Per-Page Tracking — struct page (the final goal)
Every 4KB physical page frame has a struct page describing its state.
One struct page per 4KB page frame
= millions of struct pages for GBs of RAM
Know which memory is "local" to each CPU.
Allocate from local node first = faster access.
Without this: all allocations are random = NUMA penalty.
Only allocate struct page for present memory.
Skip holes in physical address space.
Without this: waste GBs of RAM on empty page arrays.
Separate memory by DMA address constraints.
ZONE_DMA for legacy devices, ZONE_NORMAL for rest.
Without this: DMA-incapable allocs = device failures.
Every page frame tracked: who owns it, its state.
Enables buddy allocator, page cache, LRU reclaim.
All three layers above exist to build this bookkeeping.
Each step depends on the previous: NUMA topology → section allocation → zone partitioning → page tracking
After memblock_free_all(): buddy system takes over, memblock retires. Memory management is fully operational.
